source_spans.locator: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 360, published pp.815-816, Abstract/Introduction: hierarchical generative inference with context-sensitive priors
Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 360, published p.821, hierarchical empirical-Bayes section: higher-level states act as priors on lower-level states
Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 360, later cortical-physiology section: backward predictions and forward mismatch signals are iteratively reconciled

provenance.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

conditions: hierarchically organized generative inference over sensory causes
population: sensory systems modeled by the source
substrate: neighboring levels of a cortical hierarchy
task: infer latent causes of sensory input
temporal_scope: iterative recurrent exchange continues until mismatch signals are reduced

nodes.description: state at a supraordinate model level that supplies a context-dependent prior to the level below
subordinate model state constrained by both incoming data and a higher-level prior
descending estimate of the input expected at the subordinate level
difference signal between subordinate input/state and the descending estimate
current inferred state of hidden causes generating sensory input
objective of reducing weighted mismatch across model levels during inference

relations.description: the higher model level supplies a context-sensitive prior that constrains inference at the subordinate level
higher-level state generates a descending estimate of subordinate input
incompatibility between current subordinate input/state and descending estimate produces a mismatch signal
mismatch signals drive updates of higher-level cause estimates until reconciliation
the iterative inference state is selected by reducing mismatch across levels
